title: Racy worktree status cache with simulated metadata
hypothesis: An application-side status cache can miss content replacement when recorded file metadata stays equal; deterministic synthetic stat records can isolate this freshness failure.
why_hard: Metadata equality cannot always prove byte equality. A repair must reason about when a stat shortcut is trustworthy while retaining useful cache behavior.
next_action: Revisit only if reviewers accept the simulated metadata boundary as realistic paid work; otherwise seek a portable primary reproducer without host timestamp dependence.

sources.note: Recorded maintained upstream regression tests establish racy metadata as a real concern; they are not evidence that the proposed local fixture exists.

notes: Fallback candidate. Simulation weakens authenticity, while the installed-system-Git variant introduces version and filesystem sensitivity. No local trial or demonstrated model failure is recorded.
